transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well... I came in because I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It’s a nice house, it really is, it has this huge oak tree in the front yard. My wife loved it, but man, the leaves get absolutely everywhere in the fall. I spent like three hours raking last Sunday, and my neighbor, Gary, didn't even bother doing his yard, so the wind just blew them all right back into our driveway. Gary's always doing stuff like that, he’s got this old truck that leaks oil right near the property line and... sorry, I lost my train of thought. 

But yeah, the mortgage. It just feels so heavy, you know? Like every small mistake I make at the restaurant—I wait tables—it just proves I’m useless. I just feel like I deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?

Well, let's see... it’s been a while. I’d say these really low, guilty periods have been going on for about a year and two months now. Which is actually right around the time they completely overhauled the menu at the restaurant. They took off the chicken piccata, which was my absolute favorite thing to recommend. People used to come in just for that, you know? And they replaced it with this weird fusion pasta dish that nobody even knows how to pronounce. I had this one customer, this older lady with a huge hat, she got so mad at me about the menu change like I was the one back there cooking it. She left me a two-dollar tip on a sixty-dollar check. Two dollars! I mean, I get being disappointed, but it’s not my fault the owner wanted to try and be trendy. It’s just... wait, what did you ask me? Sorry, I got off track. But yeah, about a year and two months of feeling like this.

Over this past year and two months, has your low, guilty mood been present nearly every day without a break, or have there been stretches—say, a few weeks or more—when you felt back to your normal self?

Well, no, it hasn't been every single day. There was actually a stretch... maybe a few weeks, I think? Where the heavy feeling kind of lifted. I wasn't feeling so down, and I was actually getting through my shifts at the restaurant a lot better. I even picked up a couple of extra shifts because my coworker, Sarah, she had to go to her sister's wedding in Ohio. Ohio in November, can you imagine? She said it was freezing and the venue didn't have proper heating, so everyone was wearing their winter coats during the reception. And they served this dry roast beef that she said was just terrible. I always tell people, if you're going to cater a wedding, you have to do a tasting first. It's like when people order the steak well-done at my work and then complain it's tough. I mean, what do you expect? 

But anyway, yeah, I was feeling better for a few weeks there. But... even then, even when my mood was okay, I was still hearing the whispering at the house. And I still felt like I was being watched whenever I looked at the mortgage paperwork. It's like someone is just standing right over my shoulder, judging me for it.
During those few weeks when your mood felt back to normal, were you still hearing the whispering and feeling watched every day, or did those experiences go away too during that time?

Yeah, they were still there. Even when I was feeling okay, you know, not so down and getting through my shifts fine... the whispering never stopped. Every single day, I'd hear it at the condo. And the feeling of being watched, especially when I looked at the mortgage paperwork, that was still there too. It's weird because the paperwork is kept in this little home office we set up. We bought this desk from IKEA, one of those ones you have to put together yourself with the little Allen wrench? My wife and I spent an entire Saturday trying to assemble it, and we ended up putting the drawers on backwards the first time. We were so frustrated we almost just threw the whole thing out and went to get a coffee. There's this great little coffee shop down the street that makes these amazing blueberry scones. They bake them fresh every morning, and if you get there before 9 AM, they're still warm. I always try to get one on my days off, but sometimes they sell out so fast... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the whispering and feeling watched. Yeah, that didn't go away at all, even during those few weeks when my mood was better. It was just... always there.

Going back before this past year and two months, did you ever experience the whispering voices or the feeling of being watched at times when you weren't dealing with these feelings of guilt or low mood at all?

Well, yeah, actually. Before the really low, guilty stuff started... I'd say the whispering and the feeling watched started maybe two months before that? So, like, a year and four months altogether for the voices and feeling watched. I remember because it started right around the time my car broke down. It was my alternator, which is just the worst because you think it's the battery, right? You get a jump, you think you're fine, and then you're driving down the highway and all the lights on the dashboard just start flickering like a Christmas tree. I had to pull over on the shoulder of I-95 during rush hour. The tow truck driver took forever, and he had this dog in the cab with him—a little terrier mix, I think. The dog kept trying to lick my face while I was filling out the paperwork. I love dogs, but I'm actually mildly allergic, so I was sneezing the whole ride to the mechanic. And the mechanic charged me an arm and a leg, too. I should have shopped around, but when your car is dead, you just kind of go with whoever is closest. 

But yeah, anyway, the whispering and the feeling watched... that started about a year and four months ago, before the depression stuff kicked in.
During that year-plus of feeling low and guilty, did you also notice a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, along with changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels?

Well, my eating has been completely all over the place. Like, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal at work. And our staff meals are usually pretty good, actually. We have this prep cook, Hector, who makes these incredible family-meal tacos on Tuesdays. He brings in his own homemade salsa verde that his grandmother taught him how to make. He actually grows the tomatillos in his own backyard, which is crazy because I tried growing tomatoes once on my balcony and they just got completely destroyed by squirrels. Have you ever tried to keep squirrels away from a garden? It's impossible. I bought this cayenne pepper spray that was supposed to deter them, but I think they actually liked it. I swear I saw one eating a cherry tomato and licking its little paws like it was nothing. I even tried putting up this plastic owl, but the pigeons just ended up sitting on its head... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my appetite. So yeah, some weeks I barely eat at work, but then other nights I come home and just eat whatever's in the kitchen. I'll just stand there and eat anything I can find just to feel settled, you know?

I... I don't really know about all that other stuff. Like, I haven't really noticed changes with my sleep or energy, or... wait, what was the other thing? Losing interest in things? I don't know, I just... I haven't really paid attention to that. I've been so focused on the whispering and the feeling watched, you know? And the guilt just kind of sits there. But sleep and all that... I couldn't really tell you. I mean, my wife did buy us a new mattress a few months ago because she said the old one was hurting her back. We got one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box? It's wild how they fit a whole king-size mattress into a box that small. The delivery guy just left it on our porch, and it weighed like a hundred pounds. I had to drag it up the stairs by myself, and I ended up scuffing the paint on the wall in the hallway. I still haven't fixed that scuff mark, actually. I bought the paint—it's this color called "Accessible Beige," which is such a funny name for a color, right? Like, who comes up with these names? I went to the hardware store, and there's just a whole wall of paint chips with names like "Whispering Wind" or "Quiet Moment." I always wonder if that's someone's entire job, just sitting in an office naming paint colors all day. That seems like it would be a pretty relaxing job, honestly. You wouldn't have to deal with angry customers sending back their steaks because they're medium-well instead of medium... 

But yeah, anyway, I haven't really noticed any of those other things you asked about. Just the eating being all over the place.

{"intent": "Determine whether the patient has experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities, which is a core symptom needed to confirm a full major depressive episode (important for distinguishing schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia with mood symptoms

Well, I mean, I guess I have lost interest in some stuff. Like, I used to joke around a lot with the regulars at the restaurant, you know? We have this one guy, Mr. Henderson, who comes in every Thursday and orders the exact same thing—chicken piccata with extra capers. He always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts, even in the dead of winter. I asked him about it once, and he told me he buys them in bulk from this website that gets deadstock from the 90s. He said he has a whole closet just for the shirts, organized by color. I tried organizing my closet by color once, but it just lasted like two days before everything was a mess again. My wife uses those velvet hangers so the clothes don't slip off, but I find them really annoying because it's actually hard to pull the shirt off the hanger when you're in a hurry. I'm always running late for my shifts because I can never find my work shoes. 

But yeah, I don't really joke with Mr. Henderson or anyone else anymore. I just keep my face straight and say what I have to say to get the order in. And I used to text my brother after my shifts, just to decompress, but lately I just let his messages sit there. I don't even feel the pull to answer them. He sent me this video of his new puppy trying to walk on hardwood floors for the first time, and it was slipping everywhere. Hardwood floors are so tough with pets. We thought about getting laminate because it's supposed to be scratch-resistant, but then I read somewhere that it can warp if you spill water on it and don't wipe it up right away. And who has time to constantly monitor the floor for water drops, right? 

So, yeah, I guess I just don't have the energy or interest to do the things I used to do, like texting my brother or joking with the customers.

I still haven't fixed that scuff mark, actually. I bought the paint—it's this color called "Accessible Beige," which is such a funny name for a color, right? Like, who comes up with these names? I went to the hardware store, and there's just a whole wall of paint chips with names like "Whispering Wind" or "Quiet Moment." I always wonder if that's someone's entire job, just sitting in an office naming paint colors all day. That seems like it would be a pretty relaxing job, honestly. You wouldn't have to deal with angry customers sending back their steaks because they're medium-well instead of medium... 

But yeah, anyway, I haven't really noticed any of those other things you asked about. Just the eating being all over the place.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms (whispering, feeling watched) preceded mood symptoms by ~2 months and persisted daily during a multi-week euthymic period, arguing against F25.1 (which requires mood symptoms present for the majority of the illness course) and favoring F20.9. Also notable: absence of clear neurovegetative depressive symptoms (sleep/energy unaffected) and prominent tangential/circumstantial speech suggest a primary psychotic disorder with mood symptoms as a secondary feature rather than a co-primary mood component.

patient.answer:
Well, I mean, I guess I have lost interest in some stuff. Like, I used to joke around a lot with the regulars at the restaurant, you know? We have this one guy, Mr. Henderson, who comes in every Thursday and orders the exact same thing—chicken piccata with extra capers. He always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts, even in the dead of winter. I asked him about it once, and he told me he buys them in bulk from this website that gets deadstock from the 90s. He said he has a whole closet just for the shirts, organized by color. I tried organizing my closet by color once, but it just lasted like two days before everything was a mess again. My wife uses those velvet hangers so the clothes don't slip off, but I find them really annoying because it's actually hard to pull the shirt off the hanger when you're in a hurry. I'm always running late for my shifts because I can never find my work shoes. 

But yeah, I don't really joke with Mr. Henderson or anyone else anymore. I just keep my face straight and say what I have to say to get the order in. And I used to text my brother after my shifts, just to decompress, but lately I just let his messages sit there. I don't even feel the pull to answer them. He sent me this video of his new puppy trying to walk on hardwood floors for the first time, and it was slipping everywhere. Hardwood floors are so tough with pets. We thought about getting laminate because it's supposed to be scratch-resistant, but then I read somewhere that it can warp if you spill water on it and don't wipe it up right away. And who has time to constantly monitor the floor for water drops, right? 

So, yeah, I guess I just don't have the energy or interest to do the things I used to do, like texting my brother or joking with the customers.

inference.note: Patient now endorses clear anhedonia (loss of interest in joking with regulars, stopped responding to brother) plus prior confirmed guilt/worthlessness and appetite disturbance, meeting full criteria for a major depressive episode. Combined with psychotic symptoms (whispering, being watched) that began before the mood episode and persisted unchanged during a multi-week period of mood normalization, this pattern fits schizoaffective disorder (depressive type) rather than schizophrenia with mood symptoms or a mood disorder with psychotic features, so F20.9 is ruled out.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persistent auditory hallucinations ('whispering') and delusional perception of being watched/judged that began ~2 months before the onset of a major depressive episode and persisted daily even during a period of several weeks when mood symptoms remitted, establishing that psychotic symptoms occur independent of mood episodes (ruling out MDD with psychotic features). Concurrently, the patient describes a depressive syndrome lasting over a year with depressed/guilty mood, mood-congruent delusions of guilt, anhedonia (loss of interest in joking with customers, texting brother), and appetite disturbance, meeting criteria for a major depressive episode that co-occurs with the psychotic symptoms for the majority of the illness course. This combination—overlapping mood episode plus psychotic symptoms present outside the mood episode for a significant period—supports Schizoaffective Disorder, depressive type, over Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief relative to psychosis) or MDD with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes).
